newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Western managers work longer than Asians - survey.
newsitem.headline: Western managers work longer than Asians - survey.

text.p: Western managers work longer hours than their Asian counterparts, debunking a common notion that working more hours helped boost the rapid development of Asian economies, a survey made available on Friday showed.

"Findings in this study challenge the stereotype beliefs regarding the work ethics of the Western manager," said the survey by U.S.-based business consulting firm Arthur Andersen and consumer analyst Batey Research and Information Centre.
"The Western manager, on the other hand, may work longer hours in response to high unemployment rates and threats of down-sizing or corporate relocation," the report said.
The study, called "East Meets West - The Changing Faces of Management," involved 1,721 senior executives in the Asia-Pacific, Germany, France, Britain and the United States.

It found that 72 percent of Western managers work long hours compared to 64 percent of their Asian counterparts. But Western expatriates in Asia top all other senior managers, with up to 93 percent putting in longer hours at work.

The Western management style was described by respondents as being more flexible, creative, open, direct and confrontational. The Asian style was likely to be paternalistic, putting greater value on seniority, relationships and family ties.
Increased use of information technology is beginning to exert a significant impact on business in the West over the past century.
"Information technology (IT) will continue to be the driving force behind businesses. It will be a vital enabler for companies in ensuring the competitive edge," the report said.
Up to 75 percent of all respondents listed the wider use of technology to be one of three most important positive changes that will happen in their company, the report added.
"The most significant impact of IT on businesses over the past five years is the speed and efficiency (with) which work is done," it said.
